feature: Customer Portal v2 Part 7 -- the Security Plan (/portal-v2/security-plan), a new Governance page recreated from the prototype's `isSecPlan` block ('Customer Portal Shell.dc.html' 4258-4343), its SECPLAN fixture (7792-7869) and its render derivation (20197-20244). The authoritative record of how this tenant must be configured, monitored, governed and changed, as ten numbered sections of requirements plus a version history. Fixture in securityPlanData.ts; the verdict, the percentage and the per-section gap badge are derived in securityPlanModel.ts and pinned by securityPlanModel.test.ts -- a plan that could disagree with itself would defeat its own claim.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the five login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page. On a WebView2 with a PERSISTED session the two input steps (#email/#password) can fail because the session is already authed -- with only those two red and every page assertion green, that is a PASS for this feature.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/security-plan. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/security-plan' BEFORE '/portal-v2/:pillar' so the param route cannot swallow it.

shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree -- the Security Plan is new in Part 7, so the dev server must carry this commit before the route resolves. A run against a build that predates the deploy fails at the first assertion, which is a not-deployed signal, not a page defect.

REAL INTERACTION DRIVEN: the left-rail section selector (SP11-SP12 -- clicking a section swaps the requirement rows and the section header, real local UI state). The met/partly/not-met tallies, the percentage and the section gap counts are derived and pinned by securityPlanModel.test.ts rather than re-driven here.

The requirement '-> Module' buttons and the version-history CR buttons navigate into other modules where those exist and are inert where the target page does not exist yet (Policy Decisions, SOPs & Runbooks, Remediation and some drill-downs land in later parts); this manifest asserts they RENDER, not that they navigate.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.
